memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Migraine.
Patient reports recurrent unilateral throbbing headaches lasting 4-6 hours, associated with nausea and photophobia, occurring twice weekly. Neurological examination is normal. Smoking status: never (pack-years 0).

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Propranolol 40 mg OD
Sumatriptan 50 mg SOS
Topiramate 25 mg HS
Naproxen 500 mg SOS

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been having headaches three times a week now, and the sumatriptan isn’t lasting as long. I’m worried it’s getting worse.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Migraine.
Headache frequency increased to three times per week, with moderate intensity; sumatriptan used four times in past month. No new neurological deficits. Smoking status: never (pack-years 0).

memories.author: D05
memories.text:

memories.author: lab
memories.text: CBC: Hb 13.2 g/dl (12-16), WBC 6.8 x10^9/l (4-10), Plt 210 x10^9/l (150-400). ESR 8 mm/hr (0-20). Serum electrolytes within normal limits.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Migraine.
Headaches now twice weekly after topiramate discontinuation; patient reports mild tingling in fingers while on topiramate, leading to stop. Neurological exam unchanged. Smoking status: never (pack-years 0).

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Neurological examination: normal cranial nerves, no focal deficits, normal gait and coordination.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Migraine.
Headache frequency stable at twice weekly; patient reports good relief with propranolol 40 mg OD but desires better control. Neurological exam normal. Smoking status: never (pack-years 0).

Headache frequency reduced to once weekly, mild intensity; sumatriptan used twice in past month. Neurological exam normal. Smoking status: never (pack-years 0).
